title: Core existence and lifting for universal first order thickening
statement: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an $R$-algebra. Assume $R\to S$ is formally unramified, meaning that for every commutative $R$-algebra $A$ and ideal $I\subseteq A$ with $I^2=0$, composition with $q:A\to A/I$ is injective on $R$-algebra homomorphisms $S\to A$. There exist a commutative $R$-algebra $S'$ and a surjective $R$-algebra homomorphism $\pi:S'\to S$ with $(\ker\pi)^2=0$ such that for every commutative $R$-algebra $A$, square-zero ideal $I\subseteq A$, and $R$-algebra homomorphism $a:S\to A/I$, there is exactly one $R$-algebra homomorphism $a':S'\to A$ with $q\circ a'=a\circ\pi$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 04EB (lemma-universal-thickening), its statement and construction/lifting proof, without the uniqueness remark.

proof.text: Take G = Algebra.Generators.self R S and its extension P, with polynomial ring R[S], presentation map p, and kernel J. The map p is surjective by evaluating X_s to s.

Exactness of P.cotangentComplex followed by P.toKaehler, together with the subsingleton differential module of a formally unramified algebra, makes the conormal differential d surjective. The polynomial differential basis makes its target free over S. Mathlib LinearMap.exists_rightInverse_of_surjective supplies an S-linear section sigma with d composed with sigma equal to the identity.

Define N to be the range of sigma, restricted to P-scalars, Q its inverse image under J to J/J^2, and K the image of Q under the inclusion J into P. Thus K is an explicitly constructed ideal. The membership equivalence g in K iff its conormal class lies in N proves K contained in J and J^2 contained in K. Every sigma(w) has a representative g in J, giving surjectivity of the differential restricted to K. If g in K has zero differential, write its conormal class as sigma(w). Applying d shows w = 0, so the conormal class is zero and g belongs to J^2.

Define Sprime = P/K and pi = Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ K p, with well-definedness from K contained in J. Surjectivity follows from that of p. Mathlib Ideal.ker_quotient_lift identifies ker(pi) with J.map(mk K), and Ideal.map_pow identifies its square with (J^2).map(mk K), which is zero because J^2 is contained in K.

For A, I and a as in the statement, apply the polynomial correction theorem to G and K, using the two differential properties proved above. This gives a unique polynomial map beta with prescribed reduction that annihilates K. Use Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ to factor beta through P/K. The reduction equation follows by quotient algebra homomorphism extensionality and associativity. Any other quotient lift composes with the quotient map to a polynomial lift annihilating K, hence equals beta by its uniqueness; quotient extensionality gives uniqueness of the quotient lift.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_universalFirstOrderThickening_core
    (R S : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [FormallyUnramified R S] :
    ∃ (S' : Type u) (_ : CommRing S') (_ : Algebra R S') (π : S' →ₐ[R] S),
      Function.Surjective π ∧ RingHom.ker π.toRingHom ^ 2 = ⊥ ∧
      (∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] (I : Ideal A), I ^ 2 = ⊥ →
        ∀ a : S →ₐ[R] A ⧸ I,
          ∃! a' : S' →ₐ[R] A, (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R I).comp a' = a.comp π)
